sources.title: Directive (EU) 2024/2853 on liability for defective products
sources.note: Applies to products placed on the market or put into service after 9 December 2026 (Art. 2(1)). Art. 4(1) includes software in the definition of product.

sources.note: A proposal, not law. The Commission's own label is 'Digital Omnibus'; 'Data Omnibus' is informal shorthand used in this brief.

sources.publisher_name: General Court of the European Union
sources.title: Press Release No 96/26 — Joined Cases T-1079/23, T-1080/23 and T-214/24, Apple v Commission
sources.note: App Store and iOS gatekeeper designation upheld; iMessage pleas inadmissible; App Store versions treated as a single core platform service.

sources.publisher_name: General Court of the European Union
sources.title: Press Release No 114/25 — Cases T-55/24 Meta Platforms Ireland and T-58/24 TikTok Technology
sources.note: The DSA supervisory-fee implementing decisions were annulled because the methodology should have been adopted by delegated act; effects provisionally maintained for up to 12 months. This is an annulment of the fee decisions, not of the fee mechanism.

sources.title: Commission fines X EUR 120 million under the Digital Services Act
sources.note: Confirms the amount and all three grounds. Does not use the phrase 'first DSA fine'.

sources.title: EU fines X 120 million in first DSA non-compliance decision
sources.note: Carries the 'first' framing, which the Commission text does not.

sources.title: Commission fines Temu EUR 200 million for breaching the Digital Services Act
sources.note: Confirms the amount and the systemic-risk ground. Contains no ranking language; 'largest to date' is not supported by this source.

sources.title: EU tests limits of platform risk assessments with 200 million Temu fine
sources.note: Carries the 'biggest DSA penalty yet' framing.

sources.title: Commission accepts TikTok's commitments on advertising transparency under the Digital Services Act
Commission preliminarily finds TikTok's addictive design in breach of the Digital Services Act
Commission preliminarily finds addictive design on Instagram and Facebook in breach of the Digital Services Act
Commission preliminarily finds TikTok in breach of the Digital Services Act for failing to ensure safe accounts for minors
Commission finds Apple and Meta in breach of the Digital Markets Act
sources.note: EUR 500 million against Apple under Art. 5(4); EUR 200 million against Meta under Art. 5(2).

sources.title: Commission fines Google EUR 2.95 billion over abusive practices in online advertising technology
sources.note: Case AT.40670. An Article 102 TFEU antitrust decision, not a DMA decision.

sources.title: Commission refers Ireland, Spain, France and the Netherlands to the Court of Justice for failing to transpose NIS2
sources.note: Confirms the referral includes a request for financial sanctions: a lump sum and daily penalties until complete transposition is notified.

sources.title: Commission calls on 23 Member States to fully transpose the NIS2 Directive
sources.note: States that letters of formal notice went to 23 named Member States for failure to fully transpose by 17 October 2024. The figure 'only 4 of 27' is the arithmetic complement and is not stated by any official source located.

sources.title: General-Purpose AI Code of Practice
sources.note: Confirms the final version was received on 10 July 2025 and sets out the drafting timeline: first draft, second draft (19 Dec 2024), third draft (11 Mar 2025), final version (10 Jul 2025). The brief's 'after four drafts' is only accurate if the final text is counted as the fourth.

sources.title: New measures unlock access to data of the largest online platforms to support research
sources.note: Directly supports the 29 October 2025 date.

sources.title: Commission adopts delegated act on data access under the Digital Services Act
sources.note: Directly supports the centralised DSA data access portal.

sources.title: AI Omnibus enters into force
sources.note: Gives the new dates — Annex III high-risk from 2 December 2027, product-embedded high-risk from 2 August 2028 — but does not characterise the shift as 'sixteen months'. That figure is a computation, not a quoted claim.

sources.title: DMA Review Report, COM(2026) 178 final
sources.note: Supports the Article 53 basis and the enforce-rather-than-expand conclusion. Does not state the 3 May 2026 deadline or the 450-contribution figure.

sources.title: DMA review — questions and answers
sources.note: States that the first review was legally required by 3 May 2026.

sources.title: Commission publishes summary and responses to the consultation on the ongoing review of the Digital Markets Act
sources.note: Supports 'over 450 contributions'.

sources.title: Strengthening Europe's tech sovereignty
sources.note: Confirms the package date and the inclusion of the Cloud and AI Development Act. Silent on legal basis.

sources.title: ST 10104/2026 — transmission of COM(2026) 502 final, Cloud and AI Development Act
sources.note: Directly supports the dual legal basis of Article 114 TFEU and Article 173(3) TFEU applied cumulatively.
